description: Figure 3 illustrates the distribution of samples across varying levels of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity. The horizontal axis, labeled “Ambiguity std (Outer),” displays categories representing standard deviation values: 0.0, 0.47, 0.94, 1.42, and 2.0, presented as discrete categories. The vertical axis, labeled “Mode ↓,” represents the number of conversations, with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 500, incrementing by 100. Four bars are displayed for each ambiguity standard deviation category, each representing a different annotator mode: “Single-LLM” (blue), “Dual-Agent” (orange), “All” (gray), and “LLM Label Macro F1” (green). Within each standard deviation category, the bar heights are as follows: for a standard deviation of 0.0, the “Single-LLM”, “Dual-Agent”, “All”, and “LLM Label Macro F1” bars reach approximately 200, 200, 215, and 0.91, respectively; for a standard deviation of 0.47, the bar heights are approximately 300, 300, 300, and 0.47; for a standard deviation of 0.94, the bar heights are approximately 185, 185, 185, and 0.94; and for a standard deviation of 1.42, the bar heights are approximately 105, 105, 105, and 0.42. The bars are arranged in groups corresponding to each standard deviation category, and within each group, the bars are consistently ordered by the annotator mode labels. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, outlining, or annotation.
